subject: Oceanography
title: Why the Ocean Is Salty
description: A short lesson to help you apply Why the Ocean Is Salty.

hook.text: Every liter of seawater contains about 35 grams of dissolved salt—roughly one tablespoon.

buildup.text: Rivers dissolve minerals from rocks and carry them to the sea over millions of years.

discovery.text: Water evaporates from the ocean surface, but the salt stays behind—concentrating over time.

twist.text: Hydrothermal vents on the seafloor also inject minerals directly into the ocean.

climax.text: The ocean reached its current salinity billions of years ago—it's been roughly stable since.

punchline.text: Rivers bring the salt; evaporation leaves it behind.

quiz.question: Why doesn't the ocean keep getting saltier?
options: Salt is removed by geological processes at a similar rate
